thread:
Sanjay Rao: Hey team — I'm seeing a consistent mismatch between our synthetic load results and the replay runs for the microbatch SLO tests. Synthetic shows p95 ~ 60ms, replay shows p95 ~ 120ms. Any ideas?
Ellie Chen: hmm. are you replaying with the same arrival pattern? are we preserving inter-arrival jitter + client concurrency?
Sanjay Rao: Yes, using replay-tool export -> replay. We keep original timestamps. We also tried a Poisson synthetic generator with same mean qps. Still big gap.
Maya Patel: two quick suspects: KV-cache warmup/eviction behavior in replay vs synth, and kernel selection differences triggered by sequence length distributions.
Tom Brooks: +1. Also microbatch sizing: synthetic's arrivals often group into ideal microbatches, replay preserves client-side bursts that produce weird partial microbatches causing tail.
Sanjay Rao: Good point. I ran a flamegraph on the replay run — noticed spikes in kernel fallback to GEMM path at ~30% of requests, correlated with longer sequences.
PerfBot: [perf-alert] replay-run-1902468000: tail-latency spike at 1902468402, stack sample: triton_kernel_dispatch -> quantized_gemm_fallback
Jonah L.: If some requests hit quantized GEMM fallback, that could explain 2x tail. Are we pinning kernel selection in replay env?
Maya Patel: We don't force kernels on replay; runtime picks based on inferred shape + heuristic. For synthetic we were generating a narrow seq-length histogram so runtime consistently chose fused attention kernels.
Ellie Chen: So action items: (1) create a replay variant that normalizes seq-len distribution to the synthetic profile; (2) add a KV-warmup pass (replay prefix K=100 per user) to measure warmed-case; (3) capture kernel decisions per request in profiling.
Sanjay Rao: Also need to revisit percentile calculation. Right now our dashboard shows p95 across all requests for the 1h window. That conflates warmup churn. We should report rolling 5-min p95 and a cold/warm breakdown.
Tom Brooks: Agree. Plus clarify whether p99 is computed across raw latencies or per-second percentiles aggregated — mixing those is why I saw different numbers across tools.
Jonah L.: Tip: compute p95/p99 on the request-level latencies but report both the raw percentile and the 'windowed' percentile (e.g., p95 of 30s buckets). Helps spot convoys.
Maya Patel: For KV cache: replay needs to preserve cache keys affinity. If user ids are remapped or anonymized, the hotset disappears and leads to cold misses.
Sanjay Rao: Oof — we anonymize in the replay export. That likely killed locality. I'll re-run with identity-preserving option.
PerfBot: [info] run-scheduler queued replay job 1902468000-rerun-warm-kv at 1902468920
Ellie Chen: On microbatch sizing — should we expose a 'target microbatch' knob in the loadgen so we can simulate suboptimal client batching? Useful for SLO boundaries.
Tom Brooks: Yeah, and report the effective microbatch width distribution (histogram). Many of our SLO issues are when >40% of requests are singletons or small batches.
Maya Patel: Also include kernel-level metrics: which kernel used, quantization path, and whether KV cache hit/miss. Correlate with latency percentiles.
Jonah L.: One more: when we benchmark, add a controlled mix: 70% warmed, 20% cold new user, 10% long-seq tails. Synthetic-only is too clean.
Sanjay Rao: Great checklist. I'll re-run two replays: (A) identity-preserved warmup + original timestamps, (B) syntheticized seq-length + forced small microbatches. We'll capture kernel decisions and KV-hit flags.
Ellie Chen: Thanks. After runs, let's meet and decide how to represent p95/p99 in perf dashboards (raw vs windowed vs cold/warm).
Maya Patel: Quick note — measure p95 on the tail population separately (requests > token_count 256). That frequently explains regression signals we otherwise miss.
Tom Brooks: If we find kernel selection is the root cause, we might pin the fused kernel for the canary and see impact. But be careful: pinned kernels can mask future regressions if we never exercise fallback.
Sanjay Rao: Agreed. Okay re-runs queued. Will share logs + kernel decision dump when available. :thumbsup:
